checks.requirement: When a Header is decoded from a buffer, if the block's own size field decodes to a negative number, header.size becomes undefined. (the task: "the size it computes (the extended header's size, else the global extended header's size, else the block's own size field) becomes undefined if it is negative")

When a Header is constructed with { size: -1000 }, the size property stays undefined. (the task: "header data whose size is negative when compared as a number, whether passed to the constructor (new Header({ size: -1000 })) or merged in from an extended header, is ignored, so header.size stays undefined")

When Header#decode merges pax extended header data with a negative size, or global extended header data with negative size, the negative size is ignored and header.size stays as it was (from earlier sources). (the task: "header data whose size is negative when compared as a number, whether passed to the constructor (new Header({ size: -1000 })) or merged in from an extended header, is ignored, so header.size stays undefined")
A positive size passed to the Header constructor is respected. (the task: "nothing else changes")
In Pax.parse, a 'size=-1000' record leaves size undefined. (the task: "'size=-1000' ... leave size undefined")
In Pax.parse, a non-numeric 'size' value leaves size undefined. (the task: "a non-numeric value leave size undefined")
